items.headline: Flood Watch issued September 19 at 1:47PM AKDT until September 21 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
A series of low pressure systems will move through the panhandle
this weekend bringing prolonged rain combined with high freezing
levels to increase ice melt on glacier river systems. The heavy
rainfall and associated runoff will produce significant river rises
with the potential of minor flooding.

possible.

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued September 19 at 10:03AM AKDT until September 20 at 7:00AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Southeast winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts near 40 mph
expected.

* WHERE...Annette Island, Ketchikan Gateway Borough, and Prince of
Wales Island.

* WHEN...From 4 PM this afternoon to 7 AM AKDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Strongest winds will occur Saturday evening
into late Saturday night.

items.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Chena River Basin from Moose Creek Dam to the end of Chena
Hot Springs Road.

* WHEN...Until 1000 PM AKDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas. Some
low-water crossings may become impassable. River and stream flows
remain elevated. Ponding of water in areas is occurring or is
imminent.

items.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 18 at 4:14PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
ESFAFC

High water in the Kuskokwim River region will continue over the next
few days. Conditions are expected to become favorable for water
levels to gradually recede over the weekend and into the middle of
next week.

including, but not limited to: Kwethluk, Bethel, Oscarville,
